# java-guardrails 0.3.2

JaCoCo measurement now accounts for every selected module after a clean build. It uses JaCoCo's
bytecode instruction analysis to identify modules without executable code and names them as
needing no floor. Executable classes without a report produce `JACOCO_MISSING_REPORTS (decide)`
and a nonzero exit before any floors are proposed or validated. Saved floors cannot bypass it.
Missing compiled output or LINE data also stops measurement.

`assess` asks `TEST_SUPPORT_MODULES` before the first gate; direct JaCoCo measurement asks before
building too. Existing decisions retain their meaning. Gated test-support modules need their
own coverage reports: execution by downstream consumers is not aggregated back into the owner.
The measurement still runs the default `test` phase; opt-in integration tests are not activated
automatically. The stop offers own-module tests, explicit scope exclusions, or deferral for a
separately designed integration/aggregate setup. Recording a plan alone never bypasses it.

Previously recorded partial floor lists now require a completion decision when all reports are
available. Existing values are preserved. No target decisions or copied configuration are
rewritten automatically. A default floor of 1.00 alone does not make missing execution data fail
JaCoCo's Maven check; verify report completeness and falsify each claimed gate.

Real Maven fixtures cover no tests, opt-in IT only, consumer-executed test support, abstract-only
interfaces versus default methods, exclusions, partial recorded floors and compiler failures.
